title: Judgment by fire, ingathering of nations, the undying worm ↔ The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In hell the damned neither die nor live (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Judgment by fire, ingathering of nations, the undying worm: From new moon to new moon and Sabbath to Sabbath all flesh comes to worship before God; The nations bring all Israel's brothers to Jerusalem as an offering on horses, chariots, litters, mules and dromedaries; God gathers all nations and tongues to come and see his glory; God will take some of the nations as priests and Levites; God comes in fire with chariots like a whirlwind to judge all flesh by fire and sword; Those who sanctify themselves for the gardens, following one in the middle, eat swine, abominations and mice; God sends survivors to distant nations (Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, the far islands) to declare his glory; Corpses of the rebels whose worm does not die and fire is not quenched, an abhorrence to all flesh; One of the blessed recalls a companion who denied the resurrection, looks down and sees him in the midst of hell; God creates new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered; The pig is unclean and forbidden.

title: Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination ↔ Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God's throne in relation to heaven and earth [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination: The faithful are hated and cast out by their own brothers for God's name's sake; God looks to the poor and contrite in spirit who trembles at his word; 'Heaven is my throne and earth my footstool: what house could you build for me?'; Hypocritical sacrifice is equated with crimes: slaughtering an ox is like killing a man, offering a lamb like breaking a dog's neck; A tumult from the city, a voice from the temple: the voice of YHWH repaying his enemies; Those who tremble at God's word (haredim) gather to the leader.

Only in Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse: God's footstool or seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth; No compulsion in religion; Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes God; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; God does not slumber or sleep [divergence between the texts]; The guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; A day comes with no trade, no friendship and no intercession; The temple as a house of rest for the ark and the footstool of God's feet; Jesus son of Mary given clear signs and supported with the holy spirit (ruh al-qudus); Israel's God is called 'the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed'; God ranked some messengers above others; to some God spoke; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); and 4 more.

title: Cursed who trusts in man, blessed who trusts in YHWH; the deceitful heart ↔ The parable of the two gardens; this life as rain-fed plants; the book of deeds (Surah 18:32-49)

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers (weight 6.7); Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians (weight 6.7); The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho (weight 6.7); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 6.3); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 6.3). Pair score 32.6.

Only in Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety: The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate; The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm; A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God; Captive king taken with hooks and bound in bronze fetters to Babylon; Whoever surrenders to the enemy will live; his life shall be his booty.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; Famine becomes severe in the besieged city; there is no bread; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; and 2 more.

title: My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation ↔ Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether heaven and earth mourn a destroyed people [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation: The doomed city dresses in scarlet, gold ornaments and eye paint, but her lovers despise her and seek her life; Vision of the earth returned to tohu va-vohu: no light in the heavens, mountains quaking, no humans, birds fled; The people are foolish children, skilled in doing evil but not knowing how to do good; God will devastate the land but 'will not make a full end'; The prophet cries 'My bowels, my bowels! I writhe! the walls of my heart!' at the sound of war; The earth mourns and the heavens above grow dark because of God's decree; The people's terror is like the pangs of a woman in labor with her first child.

Only in Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep: The drowned Egyptians left gardens, springs, crops and noble dwellings, which God gave another people to inherit; Neither heaven nor earth wept over the destroyed people; Moses is told to leave the sea parted and still (rahwan), for Pharaoh's host will be drowned; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; Sacrificial meal eaten in haste, loins girded, sandals on, staff in hand; Who, if anyone, inherits Egypt's land after the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Why God chose Israel: love, or knowledge and testing [divergence between the texts]; God chose the Children of Israel, knowingly, above the worlds and tested them with signs; What Moses does with the sea after the crossing [divergence between the texts]; How Israel leaves Egypt by night: expelled, or secretly [divergence between the texts]; The prophet seeks refuge in God from being stoned by his people; Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'; and 2 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet reminds a disobedient people that he delivered God's message (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The remnant asks for an oracle, rejects it and drags Jeremiah to Tahpanhes; stones hidden in the pavement: The conqueror will burn the temples of a foreign land's gods; The remnant seeks safety in Egypt, where they think they will see no war nor hunger; God says he repents (nihamti) of the evil he did to his people; The conqueror breaks the obelisks (matsevot) of Beth-shemesh/Heliopolis in Egypt; The prophet's answer from God comes only after ten days; The people ask the prophet to pray for them and to tell them God's word; The people swear to obey whatever God answers, then reject the oracle; Opponents tell the prophet 'You are lying; God did not send you'; The prophet is taken down to Egypt against his counsel by the fleeing remnant; The conqueror will wrap (or pick clean) Egypt as a shepherd does his garment; The prophet buries large stones in the pavement at Pharaoh's palace where the conqueror will set his throne; The sword and famine they fear will overtake them in the very place they flee to; and 1 more.

Only in Salih, Thamud and the she-camel: The arrogant elite confront the weak (mustad'afun) who believed the prophet; The prophet turns from his destroyed people: 'I conveyed the message and advised you'; A later people (Ad, then Thamud) are made successors on the earth after a destroyed people; A people is destroyed by an earthquake/tremor (al-rajfa); A people carve houses out of the mountains and build palaces on the plains; Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'.

Pair score 17.0.

Only in Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness: The sufferer reminds God that God's hands shaped him yet now destroy him; 'Have you eyes of flesh? Are your days like a mortal's days?'; God hunts the sufferer like a lion; The underworld as a land of darkness and deep shadow, without order, where light is like darkness; God created Adam 'with my two hands'; God creates you in your mothers' bellies creation after creation in three darknesses; Like a vanishing cloud, whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up; his place knows him no more; From dust, then a drop, then a clinging clot ('alaqa), then a child, then full strength, then old age; some die before; Have you seen what you emit? evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay (weight 6.3); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 10.8.

Only in Elihu - warning dreams and the interceding angel: The healed man sings before men, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not requited to me'; The restored man's flesh becomes fresher than a child's and he returns to the days of his youth; God does all these things two or three times with a man, to bring him back from the Pit to the light of life; God speaks once, even twice, but people do not perceive it; An angel, an intercessor (malakh melits), one among a thousand, declares a man's uprightness and pleads for him; The sick man's soul draws near the Pit and his life to the 'destroyers' (memitim, angels of death); 'Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom (kofer)'; God chastens a man with pain on his bed until he loathes food and his bones stick out, as warning; 'The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of Shaddai gives me life'; In dreams during deep sleep God opens people's ears and seals their warning, to turn them from pride and spare them from the Pit; The angel of death (malak al-mawt), put in charge of humans, takes their souls; Angels glorify God and ask forgiveness for those on earth; and 4 more.

Only in Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe: Had God sent an angel he would have made him a man; Even a book on parchment they could touch would be called magic; God destroyed earlier generations though he had established them more firmly and given them rain and rivers; Praise God who created heaven and earth and made the darknesses and the light; Earlier messengers were mocked, and what the mockers mocked surrounded them; God decreed a term (ajal) for each person, and another term named with him; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; Whether darkness is made by God or exists before creation [divergence between the texts]; 'I form light and create darkness, make peace and create evil (ra'); I YHWH do all these'; God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign.

title: Elihu's hymn on rain, thunder, snow and the storm ↔ The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures

Only in Elihu's hymn on rain, thunder, snow and the storm: Golden splendor comes out of the north as God's awesome majesty; God's booth or canopy (sukkah) is made of thunderclouds and darkness; In the winter storm God seals up every man's hand (stops human work) so all may know him; The number of God's years cannot be searched out; Ice and frozen waters are produced by the breath of God; God beat out the skies hard as a molten mirror of cast metal; God draws up drops of water which distill as rain from his mist (evaporation and rainfall cycle); Storm-wind comes out of a chamber (heder) and cold from the scattering winds; God speaks to the snow 'Fall on the earth' and commands the downpour; Thunder is the roaring voice of God; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky.

title: God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens ↔ Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone (weight 6.3); God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.6.

Only in God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens: Dawn seizes the edges of the earth and shakes the wicked out of it; Light and darkness each have a dwelling place and a road to it; Rhetorical question whether rain has a father and from whose womb ice and hoarfrost are born; Lightnings sent by God report back 'Here we are'; The morning stars sing together and the sons of God shout for joy at the founding of the earth; Named constellations (Kimah/Pleiades, Kesil/Orion, Ayish/Bear, Mazzarot) and their bonds; The sea bursts out of a womb at creation and is swaddled in cloud and thick darkness; God fixes a limit, bars and doors for the sea: 'Thus far you shall come and no farther'; The springs of the sea and the recesses of the deep (tehom) as unexplored regions; The clouds are the water-skins (bottles) of heaven which God tips over; God has put wisdom in the tuhot and given understanding to the sekhvi (ibis/cock); Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; and 13 more.

Only in Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples: The companions of al-Rass (the well/pit), a destroyed people; Tall palm trees with spathes of layered dates (tal' nadid) as provision; The unbelievers marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; The people of Tubba' (the Himyarite kings of Yemen) as a destroyed people; God built the sky and adorned it, and it has no rifts (furuj); God was not wearied by creating the heavens and earth (polemic against divine rest); Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again) [divergence between the texts]; Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?'; Human comes from dust and returns to dust; and 4 more.

title: God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens ↔ The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges
summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth? (weight 6.7); Storehouses of snow and hail reserved for the day of battle (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens: Dawn seizes the edges of the earth and shakes the wicked out of it; Light and darkness each have a dwelling place and a road to it; Rhetorical question whether rain has a father and from whose womb ice and hoarfrost are born; Lightnings sent by God report back 'Here we are'; The morning stars sing together and the sons of God shout for joy at the founding of the earth; Named constellations (Kimah/Pleiades, Kesil/Orion, Ayish/Bear, Mazzarot) and their bonds; The sea bursts out of a womb at creation and is swaddled in cloud and thick darkness; God fixes a limit, bars and doors for the sea: 'Thus far you shall come and no farther'; The springs of the sea and the recesses of the deep (tehom) as unexplored regions; The clouds are the water-skins (bottles) of heaven which God tips over; God has put wisdom in the tuhot and given understanding to the sekhvi (ibis/cock); God challenges the human: 'Gird your loins like a man; I will question you and you inform me'; and 13 more.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; Dream of a ladder or stairway reaching heaven with angels ascending and descending; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; The blessed recline on couches set in rows (or face to face); and 12 more.

matches.note: A thing that cannot speak becomes a witness: hā-ʾeḇen ha-zōʾṯ tihyeh bānû lə-ʿēḏâ kî hîʾ šāməʿâ ʾēṯ kol ʾimrê YHWH ... pen təḵaḥăšûn bē-ʾlōhêḵem vs. shahida ʿalayhim ... julūduhum; anṭaqanā llāh. Hag 16a (a man's limbs testify against him, citing Isa 43:12), not in the HB itself.

summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Lev 11 forbids many species and treats contact with nəbēlâ as defiling (hannōgēaʿ bənibəlātāh yiṭmāʾ ... wəhāʾōkēl minnibəlātāh yəkabbēs bəgādāyw). matches.label: List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness')
matches.note: Lev 18:7-17 ʿerwat ... lōʾ tĕgallēh: mother, father's wife, sister and half-sister, granddaughter, aunts, uncle's wife, daughter-in-law, brother's wife, a woman with her daughter; Q 4:23 ḥurrimat ʿalaykum ummahātukum wa-banātukum wa-akhawātukum wa-ʿammātukum wa-khālātukum wa-banātu l-akhi wa-banātu l-ukhti wa-ummahātukumu llātī arḍaʿnakum wa-akhawātukum mina r-raḍāʿa ...: mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, nieces, nursing mothers and milk sisters, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters, sons' wives. title: Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen ↔ Usury

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

title: Priests who despise God's name with blemished offerings ↔ Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: From sunrise to sunset God's name is great among the nations and in every place incense and a pure offering are brought to his name (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

title: YHWH's lawsuit with his people; what YHWH requires ↔ The clear proof
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: What God requires: to do justice, love hesed and walk humbly with your God (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in YHWH's lawsuit with his people; what YHWH requires: Remember what Balak king of Moab plotted and how Balaam son of Beor answered him; God sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before the people (Miriam named as a leader); God's plea: 'My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me'; Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression? Thousands of rams and rivers of oil do not please God; God offered the Trust (amana) to the heavens, earth and mountains; they refused and feared it, but man bore it, unjust and ignorant; God desires a broken spirit, thanksgiving or obedience rather than animal sacrifice; God summons heaven and earth to the judgment of his people in a covenant lawsuit.

Only in The clear proof: God is pleased with the saved and they are pleased with him; The People of the Book split only after the clear proof (al-bayyina) came to them; A messenger from God recites purified scrolls (suhuf mutahhara) containing upright writings; They were commanded only to serve God sincerely, as hunafa' (pure monotheists), pray and give alms: the upright religion; The reward of the righteous is the gardens of Eden (jannat 'adn) beneath which rivers flow, forever.

title: No godly man left; who is a God like you? ↔ Al-Taghabun: forms made beautiful, the Day of Mutual Loss, enemies among wives and children, and the goodly loan
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own household (weight 6.7); Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own household [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in No godly man left; who is a God like you?: 'Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: though I fall I shall rise; though I sit in darkness YHWH is my light'; The godly have vanished from the land like a vineyard after gleaning with no cluster to eat; God will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea; Trust no neighbor or friend; guard your mouth even from the wife in your bosom; God will show truth to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham as he swore to the fathers; Enemies bow down and lick the dust before the king or God; 'Lay your hand upon your mouth': gesture of appalled silence; Nations taunt 'Where is their God?'; God called the patriarch's shepherd all his life; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Al-Taghabun: forms made beautiful, the Day of Mutual Loss, enemies among wives and children, and the goodly loan: The Day of Gathering is the Day of Mutual Dispossession / Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun); Among your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them; yet if you pardon and forgive, God is forgiving; Fear God as much as you are able (ma stata'tum); No calamity strikes except by God's leave; whoever believes, God guides his heart; Unbelievers rejected their messengers saying 'Shall mere humans guide us?'; God created you, and among you are unbelievers and believers; God shaped you and made your forms good (sawwarakum fa-ahsana suwarakum); The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; The Day of Gathering (yawm al-jam') when all humanity is assembled; one party to the Garden, one to the Blaze; Wealth and children are a trial (fitna); The prophet is not a guardian over people; his duty is only to deliver the message (al-balagh); God is the Rich (al-ghani) and you are the poor; the miser is miserly only against himself; and 5 more.

matches.label: Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt
matches.note: Num 11:5 zākarnû ʾet ha-ddāgâ ... ʾēt ha-qqiššuʾîm wĕ-ʾēt hā-ʾăbaṭṭiḥîm wĕ-ʾet he-ḥāṣîr wĕ-ʾet ha-bbĕṣālîm wĕ-ʾet ha-ššûmîm; Q 2:61 baqlihā wa-qiththāʾihā wa-fūmihā wa-ʿadasihā wa-baṣalihā. Three cognates (qiššuʾîm / qiththāʾ, bĕṣālîm / baṣal, šûmîm / fūm). Changed: in Numbers the craving is for meat (mî yaʾăkilēnû bāśār, 11:4) and the food is remembered from Egypt; in the Quran the complaint is 'one food' (lan naṣbira ʿalā ṭaʿāmin wāḥidin), fish and meat are absent, lentils are added. The outcome changes too: plague in Num 11:33; in Q ihbiṭū miṣran fa-inna lakum mā saʾaltum, and humiliation.

title: Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail ↔ The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna

Only in Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail: Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint; Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically); A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin; Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets'; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' matches.note: Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. matches.note: Inheritance of a man with no child. Num: ʾîš kî-yāmût û-vēn ʾên lô ... lə-vittô; wə-ʾim-ʾên lô bat ... lə-ʾeḥāyw, then the father's brothers and the nearest kin. Only in War against Midian and division of the spoils: Five named kings slain together; Captured gold jewelry offered to atone for the soldiers' lives; Leader given a final task to complete before he is 'gathered to his people'; Commanders report that not one man of the army is missing; Priest accompanies the army with holy vessels and trumpets; Metal spoils purified by passing through fire, others through water; Warriors and captives purified outside camp seven days after battle; Army of a thousand from each tribe (12,000); How the people of Midian came to be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; God punishes the enemy by the believers' hands and heals the believers' breasts; God commands war of vengeance against a people; Foreign seer blamed for advising the seduction that led to apostasy; and 5 more.

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; Cities 'great and fortified up to heaven'; Do not cut down fruit trees during a siege: is the tree of the field a man?; Opening formula: whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God (sabbaha / yusabbihu lillah); and 1 more.

matches.note: Sharing out spoil. Numbers: wə-ḥāṣîṯā ʾeṯ ham-malqôaḥ bên tōp̄śê ham-milḥāmâ ... û-ḇên kol hā-ʿēḏâ, wa-hărēmōṯā meḵes la-YHWH, given to Eleazar the priest (half to the fighters, half to the people, a levy for God through the priest). Quran: mā afāʾa llāhu ʿalā rasūlihi ... fa-mā awjaftum ʿalayhi min khaylin wa-lā rikāb ... fa-li-llāhi wa-li-r-rasūli wa-li-dhī l-qurbā wa-l-yatāmā wa-l-masākīni wa-bni s-sabīli kay lā yakūna dūlatan bayna l-aghniyāʾi minkum. Spoil taken without fighting gives the fighters no share: all goes to God, the Prophet, kin and the needy, so that wealth does not circulate among the rich. The priest's levy becomes the Prophet's share.

title: The suspected adulteress and the bitter water ↔ Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath
summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Adultery done in secret with no witness and not caught in the act (weight 6.7); Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); How the case of a wife suspected of adultery is decided [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal (weight 6.7). Pair score 33.5.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven.

Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; The penalty for adultery or fornication [contrast between the texts]; The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity [divergence between the texts]; Husband who falsely accuses his bride is flogged, fined 100 silver, and may never divorce her; Adulterer and adulteress both put to death; and 3 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts]; Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven; and 3 more.

matches.label: When a consecrated person shaves the head
matches.note: Num 6:5, 18 taʿar lōʾ yaʿăbōr ʿal rōʾšô ... wĕ-gillaḥ ha-nnāzîr petaḥ ʾōhel môʿēd ... wĕ-nātan ʿal hā-ʾēš ʾăšer taḥat zebaḥ ha-ššĕlāmîm: hair uncut during the vow, shaved at the sanctuary at its end and burned under the offering; Q 2:196 wa-lā taḥliqū ruʾūsakum ḥattā yablugha l-hadyu maḥillahu: no shaving in the pilgrim state until the offering reaches its place. The shaving tied to the offering is kept; the hair is not burned, and the rule applies to every pilgrim, not to a private vow.

passages.text: כָּל יְמֵי֙ נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔וֹ תַּ֖עַר לֹא יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל רֹאשׁ֑וֹ עַד מְלֹ֨את הַיָּמִ֜ם אֲשֶׁר יַזִּ֤יר לַיהוָה֙ קָדֹ֣שׁ יִהְיֶ֔ה גַּדֵּ֥ל פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁוֹ
וְגִלַּ֣ח הַנָּזִ֗יר פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶת רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ וְלָקַ֗ח אֶת שְׂעַר֙ רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֔וֹ וְנָתַן֙ עַל הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּ֖חַת זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים

وَأَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلْحَجَّ وَٱلْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْىِ وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا۟ رُءُوسَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْهَدْىُ مَحِلَّهُۥ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ بِهِۦٓ أَذًى مِّن رَّأْسِهِۦ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمْ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى ٱلْحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْىِ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِى ٱلْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُۥ حَاضِرِى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ

matches.label: One with an ailment of the head pays ransom by fasting, alms or sacrifice
matches.note: Num 6:9-10 wĕ-kî yāmût mēt ʿālāyw ... wĕ-gillaḥ rōʾšô ... yābiʾ šĕtê tōrîm ʾô šĕnê bĕnê yônâ: if the consecrated head is defiled he shaves early and brings an offering; Q 2:196 fa-man kāna minkum marīḍan aw bihi adhan min raʾsihi fa-fidyatun min ṣiyāmin aw ṣadaqatin aw nusuk: one forced to shave early because of a head ailment pays by fasting, alms or a sacrifice. Early shaving of a consecrated head, made good by an offering; the Quran gives three options.

title: The Nazirite vow ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
summary: 1 shared motif, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The Nazirite vow: Priest places the boiled shoulder and cakes in the hands of the shaved Nazirite and waves them; Nazirite may not become unclean even for the corpse of father, mother, brother or sister; A man or a woman may take the vow of a Nazirite; Sudden death of someone beside a Nazirite voids his vow and he must start again; After the vow's completion rite the Nazirite may drink wine; Abstinence from wine, by vow or by general law [divergence between the texts]; One with an ailment of the head pays ransom by fasting, alms or sacrifice; Nazirite abstains from wine, vinegar, grapes and everything from the vine down to seeds and skins; Nazirite's shaved hair is put on the fire under the well-being offering; When a consecrated person shaves the head [divergence between the texts]; The consecrated person lets his hair grow uncut as the sign of his vow; Two turtledoves or two young pigeons offered (in place of a lamb if one cannot afford it).

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; Who chose or founded the single sanctuary of sacrifice, and when [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

matches.label: Abstinence from wine, by vow or by general law
matches.note: Abstention from wine. Num: by vow, as a mark of holiness (mi-yyayin wə-šēkhār yazzîr), and the Nazirite brings a ḥaṭṭāʾt, wə-khipper ʿālāyw mēʾăšer ḥāṭāʾ ʿal-ha-nnāfeš. Q forbids self-imposed abstinence (lā tuḥarrimū ṭayyibāti mā aḥalla llāhu lakum, 5:87), yet makes wine itself rijsun min ʿamali l-shayṭāni for all (5:90). cf. (not a match) b. Taʿanit 11a, which reads Num 6:11 as the sin of self-denial.

title: Sayings on the tongue, the strong tower and the lot ↔ Al-Hujurat: lowering voices, verifying reports, reconciling believers, backbiting and the peoples and tribes
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Slander or gossip pictured as eating [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The words of a whisperer are like delicious morsels that go down into the inner chambers of the belly (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Sayings on the tongue, the strong tower and the lot: He who answers before he hears, it is folly and shame to him; Death and life are in the hand of the tongue; There is a friend who sticks closer than a brother; A man's gift makes room for him and brings him before the great; The first to plead his case seems right until the other comes and examines him; The lot puts an end to quarrels and decides between the mighty; The name of YHWH is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is safe; An offended brother is harder to win than a strong city; quarrels are like the bars of a citadel; The words of a man's mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom a gushing stream; He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from YHWH; a prudent wife is from YHWH; He who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous are both an abomination to YHWH; Before honor comes humility; and 5 more.

Only in Al-Hujurat: lowering voices, verifying reports, reconciling believers, backbiting and the peoples and tribes: Those who call the prophet from outside his private chambers (hujurat) lack understanding; they should wait until he comes out; They count their submission a favor to the prophet; rather God has done them a favor in guiding them; Let no people mock another, nor women other women, nor defame one another or insult with nicknames; If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them; fight the one that transgresses until it returns to God's command; The bedouin say 'we believe'; rather say 'we have submitted (aslamna)', for faith has not yet entered your hearts; The believers are nothing but brothers, so make peace between your brothers; One origin (one father, one pair, one God) as ground for conduct toward others [divergence between the texts]; Believers must not put themselves before God and his messenger, nor raise their voices above the prophet's or shout to him; Humanity created from a male and a female and made into peoples (shu'ub) and tribes to know one another; the noblest is the most pious; 'Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously with one another?'; If a corrupt person brings you news, verify it lest you harm a people in ignorance and come to regret it; Avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting: would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?; and 3 more.

Only in End of the first Solomonic collection (good name, training a child): The rich rules the poor and the borrower is slave to the lender; Train up a child according to his way; when he is old he will not depart from it; He who oppresses the poor insults his Maker; he who is gracious to the needy honors him; The prudent sees evil and hides; the simple go on and suffer for it; Rich and poor meet together; YHWH is the maker of them all; The sluggard says 'There is a lion outside; I shall be killed in the streets'; The mouth of the strange woman (or harlot) is a deep pit, a narrow well into which the cursed falls; Before honor comes humility; The 'good of eye' (generous) is blessed; the 'evil of eye' (stingy, envious) is to be shunned; Friend's doctrine: no innocent man ever perished; those who plow iniquity reap it; He who spares the rod hates his son; corporal discipline of children is commended.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The effects of wine on the drinker [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Those who linger over wine; 'My son, give me your heart and let your eyes keep my ways'; Do not be among wine-bibbers and gluttonous eaters of meat, for drunkard and glutton come to poverty and rags; The harlot lies in wait like a robber and multiplies the faithless among men; The speaker's kidneys (kilyot) exult at the son's upright words; Do not envy sinners or evildoers, for there is a future (aharit) and your hope will not be cut off; The mouth of the strange woman (or harlot) is a deep pit, a narrow well into which the cursed falls; Do not look at wine when it is red and sparkles in the cup; at the last it bites like a serpent and stings like a viper; The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none [contrast between the texts]; A wise son gladdens his father; a foolish son grieves his mother.

title: 'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field ↔ Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether one may pay back a wrong in kind [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Do not say 'I will do to him as he has done to me; I will pay the man back for his deed' (weight 6.7). Pair score 13.4.

Only in 'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field: He who gives an honest answer kisses the lips; Prepare your work outside and get your field ready; afterwards build your house; The wise man passes the field of the sluggard, overgrown with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down, and draws a lesson; Showing partiality in judgment is not good; he who tells the wicked 'you are righteous' is cursed by peoples; 'A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands', and poverty comes like a vagabond, want like an armed man; A collection introduced as 'words of (or sayings belonging to) the wise'; A faithful witness does not lie; a false witness breathes out lies and will not go unpunished.

Only in Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon: The believers conduct their affairs by mutual consultation (shura); God has dispersed living creatures (dabba) in both the heavens and the earth and can gather them; God accepts repentance from his servants and pardons evil deeds; Retaliation in kind is permitted, but whoever pardons and makes peace has his reward with God; God's control of the wind over ships at sea: raising a storm or stilling it [divergence between the texts]; Whatever misfortune strikes people is for what their own hands have earned, though God pardons much; What is given in this life is passing enjoyment (mata'); what is with God is better and more lasting; God sends down rain after people have despaired and spreads out his mercy; Ships running on the sea like landmarks/mountains are a sign; God could still the wind and leave them motionless or wreck them; If God gave his servants unlimited provision they would transgress on earth, so he sends down in measure; Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis) [divergence between the texts]; Without counsel a people falls; in a multitude of counselors there is victory; and 1 more.

title: Words of Agur son of Yakeh, confession of ignorance and prayer ↔ Sad: the chiefs marvel at one God; the confederates of old
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: If they own heaven and earth, let them ascend by the cords or ways (asbab) to heaven (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Words of Agur son of Yakeh, confession of ignorance and prayer: Do not add to his words lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar; Every word of God is refined (tested); he is a shield to those who take refuge in him; Riddle question about God (the creator): 'What is his name, and what is the name of his son?'; Prayer for two things: keep falsehood far and give neither poverty nor riches, only my allotted bread, lest I deny God or steal; The sage declares himself more brutish than any man, without human understanding or knowledge of the Holy One; Sayings attributed to Agur son of Yakeh, an oracle (massa) addressed to Ithiel and Ucal; Who has gone up to heaven and come down, gathered the wind in his fists, wrapped the waters in a garment? What is his name and his son's name?; Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm.

Only in Sad: the chiefs marvel at one God; the confederates of old: Opponents say 'We did not hear of this in the latest religion (al-milla al-akhira); it is a fabrication'; The chiefs marvel 'Has he made the gods one God?' and urge each other to stay patient with their gods; Pharaoh 'possessor of the stakes' (dhu al-awtad); Opponents ask whether the prophet has forged a lie against God or is possessed (bihi jinna); Destroyed generations cried out when it was no longer a time for escape (lata hina manas); Scoffers ask 'Lord, hasten to us our share (qittana) before the Day of Reckoning'; Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished; List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

title: Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures) ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ant, a people without strength, prepares its food in summer (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures): The adulteress eats, wipes her mouth and says 'I have done no wrong'; Pressing milk produces butter, pressing the nose produces blood, pressing anger produces strife (pun on af 'nose/anger'); Do not slander a slave to his master lest he curse you; Four small but wise creatures: ants storing food in summer, rock-badgers housed in rock, locusts with no king marching in ranks, the lizard in kings' palaces; Four stately in stride: the lion mightiest of beasts, the strutting rooster (zarzir), the he-goat, and a king with his army; Under four the earth trembles: a slave who becomes king, a fool sated with food, an unloved woman who marries, a maid who supplants her mistress; Catalogue of a corrupt 'generation' (dor): cursing parents, self-righteous yet unwashed, haughty, with sword-teeth devouring the poor; If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, put your hand on your mouth; The leech ('aluqah) has two daughters: 'Give, give!'; The locusts have no king yet all go out in ranks; The eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother will be pecked out by ravens of the valley and eaten by young vultures; Four wonders: the way of an eagle in the sky, a serpent on a rock, a ship in the sea, and a man with a young woman ('almah); and 4 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

title: Proverbs 4, a father's father's teaching; the two paths ↔ The Opening (al-Fatiha)
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Contrast of the way of the righteous, which God knows, and the way of the wicked, which perishes (weight 6.0); Prayer to be guided on the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim) (weight 5.8). Pair score 11.8.

Only in Proverbs 4, a father's father's teaching; the two paths: 'The beginning of wisdom: acquire wisdom; with all you have acquired, acquire understanding'; The wicked cannot sleep unless they do evil; they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence; Guard your heart above all, for from it are the issues (springs) of life; The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn growing brighter to full day; the way of the wicked is deep darkness; Teacher recalls being a tender only son taught by his own father, passing the teaching to his sons; Love Wisdom and embrace her; she will exalt you and set on your head a garland and a crown of glory; Keeping the teaching brings length of days, years of life and peace; Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; Wisdom (hokhmah) personified as a woman who speaks in the first person.

title: Proverbs 6:20-35, commandment as lamp; adultery as fire in the bosom ↔ Luqman's advice to his son
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How far a child must obey father and mother [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); 'Hear, my son, your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching (torah)' (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Proverbs 6:20-35, commandment as lamp; adultery as fire in the bosom: 'The commandment is a lamp and the teaching (torah) is light; reproofs of discipline are the way of life'; Can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not burn, or walk on coals and his feet not be scorched? So is adultery; A prostitute costs a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts the precious life; The jealous husband shows no mercy on the day of vengeance and will accept no ransom (kofer) or bribe for adultery; When you walk it will lead you, when you lie down it will watch over you, when you wake it will talk with you; A starving thief is not despised, yet when caught he repays sevenfold, giving all the wealth of his house; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden; The Torah contains guidance and light; Bind the teachings around your neck (or fingers) and write them on the tablet of your heart; Warning against the 'strange woman' (ishah zarah / nokhriyyah) with smooth words.

Only in Luqman's advice to his son: Do not turn your cheek away from people in scorn or walk proudly on the earth; be modest in your walk; Associating partners with God (shirk) is a tremendous wrong; Lower your voice: the most repugnant of voices is the braying of donkeys; Luqman, a sage given wisdom by God, instructs his son; The mother carried the child in weakness upon weakness and his weaning is in two years; Even a deed the weight of a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or in heaven or earth, God will bring it forth; A community that enjoins the good and forbids the evil (al-amr bil-ma'ruf); How to treat close kin who urge one to worship other gods [contrast between the texts]; Children must treat parents well but must not obey them if they press them to associate partners with God; Whether the heavens rest on pillars [divergence between the texts]; God raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; God set firm mountains on the earth lest it sway with people; and 4 more.

matches.note: Parental authority. Prov: nəṣōr bənî miṣwaṯ ʾāḇîḵā wə-ʾal-tiṭṭōš tôraṯ ʾimmeḵā, binding without condition. Q: wa-waṣṣaynā l-insāna bi-wālidayhi ... wa-in jāhadāka ʿalā an tushrika bī ... fa-lā tuṭiʿhumā wa-ṣāḥibhumā fī d-dunyā maʿrūfan. The duty to parents is commanded by God, not by the father, and it stops where the parents urge shirk. title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs
summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God lays the beams of his upper chambers on the (heavenly) waters and waters the mountains from them (weight 6.7); All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs: Every creature on earth has its provision from God, who knows its resting place and depository; Before creation God's throne was upon the water; On judgment day witnesses (al-ashhad) testify against those who lied about God; Those who want only this life are paid in full here and have nothing in the hereafter but fire; God created heaven and earth to test which of you is best in deeds; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; YHWH sat enthroned over the flood (mabbul); YHWH sits as king forever; Man calls on God lying, sitting or standing in distress, then passes on as if he had never prayed once relieved; Moses writes the Torah and gives it to the Levitical priests and elders; What is over the waters before or at creation: God's spirit, his throne or his voice [divergence between the texts]; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?'; and 9 more.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.
